name: 2D Survivors Roguelike
agentBrief: A complete survivors-like: you move, weapons fire themselves, and you draft upgrades until the build snowballs (Godot 4.6, GDScript). SCENE FLOW: res://scenes/main_menu.tscn (entry) -> res://scenes/character_select.tscn -> res://main.tscn. NOTE main.tscn IS AT THE REPO ROOT, not in scenes/ — every other scene is under scenes/, so do not go hunting there for the gameplay scene. PLAYER: scripts/player.gd on scenes/player.tscn (CharacterBody2D). Eight-directional movement, position hard-clamped to +/-1500. Damage funnels through apply_hit(amount) with a 2s invulnerability timer — use that gate, not take_damage(), for anything that should respect i-frames. apply_character(cfg) reconfigures max health, speed, magnet radius and SpriteFrames from the chosen character. Animations are walk_right/walk_up/walk_down with flip_h for leftward travel; THERE IS NO SEPARATE LEFT ANIMATION SET. INPUT IS HARDCODED: there is NO [input] section in project.godot at all — player.gd reads Input.is_physical_key_pressed(KEY_W/A/S/D) directly, and main.gd reads KEY_L (debug level-up), KEY_B, KEY_ESCAPE, KEY_R. Adding gamepad or rebindable controls means building the input map from scratch. TOUCH: scripts/virtual_joystick.gd is a floating on-screen stick that main.gd adds to the UI layer at runtime; it listens to InputEventScreenTouch/Drag only, so a desktop mouse never triggers it and the keyboard stays the sole desktop input. It publishes a movement vector through the 'joystick' group, which player.gd reads — keep that group name if you move it. WEAPONS: scripts/weapon_system.gd fires everything automatically on per-weapon cooldowns — there is NO manual attack input. Weapons are data-driven via scripts/weapon_def.gd (class_name WeaponDef, a Resource: fire_rate, targeting_mode CLOSEST_ENEMY or RANDOM_DIRECTION, damage, projectile_speed, homing, lifetime, explosion_radius, dies_on_wall, bounce_count). Only two defs exist: resources/weapons/homing_missile.tres and random_missile.tres. Defs are duplicate()d on load so upgrades never mutate the cached resource — preserve that. Two non-projectile systems: scripts/saw_system.gd (orbiting blades on tethers) and scripts/lightning_system.gd (zaps random enemies every 4s). Targeting is scripts/targeting.gd, a static closest_enemy() doing a linear scan of the 'enemies' group. UPGRADES: the pool is a hardcoded const UPGRADES array of 11 entries in scripts/main.gd (ids: missiles, homing, speed, maxhp, xprate, regen, explode, bounce, saw, lightning, flaming) with _apply_upgrade/_desc_for/_stacks alongside it. Three random cards per level-up, gated by max_stacks, needs_weapon and needs_special. ADDING CONTENT MEANS EDITING THAT ARRAY IN main.gd — it is not resource-driven, and there is no reroll, banish or rarity system. LEVELING: scripts/level_system.gd, linear curve needed = 5 + (level-1)*3; XP comes from scripts/xp_gem.gd gems that idle until the player magnet calls attract_to(). DIFFICULTY SCALES OFF PLAYER LEVEL, NOT TIME: enemy_spawner.gd recomputes spawn_interval = max(0.2, 1.5 * pow(0.887, level-1)) on every level-up. The ONLY time-based system is scripts/boss_system.gd — first boss at 120s then every 120s, HP 500 + 100*level. survival_time is displayed but drives nothing. ENEMIES: three scenes (enemy, enemy_fast, enemy_giant) all sharing scripts/enemy.gd — straight-line chase, contact damage, knockback with decay, a spawn grow-in during which they are harmless. Mix is 5/25/70 giant/fast/normal. BOSS: scripts/boss.gd is a real state machine (stalk, charge-wind, charge, jump-wind, jump-air, jump-land, barrage, recover) with telegraph nodes. CHARACTERS: scripts/run_state.gd holds two — 'rogue' (DISPLAYED AS 'Mage' — the id and label disagree, do not assume they match) and 'knight'. run_state.gd is a static var on a preloaded script, deliberately NOT an autoload, so it needs no project reload. UI: everything is under the UI CanvasLayer in main.tscn EXCEPT the pause menu, which main.gd builds procedurally in _build_pause_menu() — you will not find it in the .tscn. AUDIO: scripts/sfx.gd is the only autoload, a 16-voice round-robin pool. CAUTION: its SOUNDS keys 'arrow_shoot' and 'orb_cast' are cross-wired to each other's files, and weapon_system.gd inverts them a second time, so the audible result is correct by accident — fixing one side alone WILL break it. NO SAVE SYSTEM EXISTS: no FileAccess, ConfigFile, user:// or JSON anywhere, so no high scores, meta-progression or persisted settings. ART: .summer/art-bible.md is the accurate style reference and locks a 'Don't Starve woodcut' dark-painterly look — read it before generating any new art. docs/ is STALE (it describes a v1 that shipped code has long since superseded); trust the scripts and the art bible over docs/. CUSTOMIZE BY: adding WeaponDef resources, extending the UPGRADES array, adding enemy scenes on enemy.gd, retuning the boss state machine — do not rewrite the weapon_system/level_system spine.

userFacing.tagline: Weapons fire themselves. You dodge, level up, and draft upgrades until the screen is yours.
highlights: Automatic weapons with homing missiles, wall-bouncing arrows, orbiting saws and chain lightning
Endless enemy spawning that tightens as you level
Draft one of three upgrades on every level-up, from a pool of eleven that stack and gate each other
A telegraphed boss that returns every two minutes and scales with you
Two playable characters with different health, speed, starting weapons and an exclusive upgrade
Three enemy types, knockback, damage numbers, hit flashes and camera shake
Plays on touch devices too, with a floating on-screen joystick
Hand-styled woodcut art with a documented art bible to match when you add more
